card.category: former premium file host, now a redirect to DDownload
card.summary: Not applicable: ddl.to serves no offer of its own. The domain redirects to ddownload.com.

record.category: former premium file host, now a redirect to DDownload

free_tier.stated: Not applicable: ddl.to serves no offer of its own. The domain redirects to ddownload.com.
free_tier.notes: The successor's terms belong to storage/ddownload and are not restated here.

per_object_cap.stated: Not applicable: the brand no longer hosts.

egress.terms: None from this domain; every request is forwarded to ddownload.com.

record.interface_detail: An HTTP redirect. There is no endpoint to call.
record.tooling: Nothing to tool against. A client that still holds a ddl.to link is handed to DDownload's own page.
record.chaining: A dead link in old index posts. Its only use now is to know that a DDL.to URL still resolves, to DDownload, rather than 404ing - so a link checker will report it alive when the host behind it is a different company.
record.limits_note: No constraint applies to a redirect.
record.binding_note: Nothing transfers from this domain, so nothing can bind.

identity_cost.detail: Nothing is asked for at ddl.to; whatever the redirect target asks for is DDownload's policy.

record.reliability_note: A link checker sees HTTP 200 and a live host, which is exactly the failure these records warns about: the host answering is not the host the link names. Any inventory that still counts DDL.to as a separate provider is double-counting DDownload.
record.confidence_note: The redirect and its landing page were read. That is all this record claims.

evidence.proved: ddl.to resolves to https://ddownload.com/ and serves the DDownload homepage ('Ultimate Cloud Storage - DDownload'), so the brand is retired and the domain forwards

record.notes: Kept as a dead record rather than deleted so the subsequent audit does not re-open the name and so the DDownload redirect is documented once. Successor: storage/ddownload.
